profile: Has studied Japanese for eight years and holds the JLPT N3.

availability.headline: Available all year round
availability.text: From March 2027. Travels in every season at two weeks’ notice. Prefers seasonal contracts. Passport valid until 2 May 2033.

highlights.title: Two trips
highlights.text: To Japan, both planned by himself

experience.intro: Boutique travel agency designing private trips for clients from Canada and Australia.
bullets: Private itineraries across Greece, Cyprus and Malta: 25 to 40 a year, usually 7 to 12 days long.
Takes each client from the first call to the flight home: needs interview, written proposal, day-by-day itinerary, bookings.
Books hotels, licensed guides, private drivers, yacht days, ferries and domestic flights for programmes with several stops.
Writes the final trip book (contacts, transfer times, confirmations) and reconfirms every service a week before arrival.
Records dietary needs and mobility limits, checks visa rules, and adds a café and taverna list for each stop.

support.text: On call during every trip as the clients’ single contact with local suppliers.

cases.text: a gale kept the clients’ catamaran in port. He moved them to the next morning’s ferry, extended their room by one night and moved their farewell dinner booking.
a client lost her passport two days before departure. He booked an emergency passport appointment, changed her flight and kept the rest of the party on their original plan.

bullets: Call centre for a regional airline: answering passengers, bookings, seat and baggage changes on the Amadeus and Sabre systems.

story.title: Planning the 18-day trip
story.subtitle: October 2024 · himself and four colleagues
items: The whole route from scratch: rail passes, hotels, a day plan for each city.
Travel insurance and passport checks for the group; mobile data for every phone.
Luggage sent ahead from Kanazawa to Nikko (takkyubin), booked in Japanese.
Every hotel booked with free cancellation until three days before arrival.
When a typhoon cancelled the trains north of Sendai, he moved the group to the next morning’s service and one hotel night with it, and no stop was dropped.
In Shirakawa-go the last bus back was full. He booked a farmhouse stay in the village by phone, in Japanese, and moved the Nagoya visit to the next afternoon.
